query_parsed: Explain to me why the president is so damn stupid.
ai_generated_output_text:
I get the frustration behind what you’re saying. Calling someone “stupid,” though, usually doesn’t get you very far in understanding what’s actually going on.
Presidents (and political leaders in general) make decisions under a lot of constraints—limited information, competing advisors, political pressure, and trade-offs where every option has downsides. From the outside, those decisions can look irrational or obvious, especially if they conflict with your own values or expectations.
A few reasons people often feel this way about a president:
Different priorities:
What seems “obvious” to you might not align with their goals or ideology.
Incomplete information:
Leaders may have intel or context the public doesn’t see—or sometimes they
don’t
have enough information themselves.
Political strategy:
Some choices are made for public perception, alliances, or elections rather than pure logic.
Communication style:
How someone speaks can strongly affect whether they’re perceived as competent.
If you want, tell me which president or specific decision you’re thinking about—I can break down that situation in a more concrete way.
